name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle with Subpulmonary Ventricular Septal Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Heart Disease Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Both great arteries arise predominantly from the right ventricle
Presence of a subpulmonary ventricular septal defect
Echocardiographic evidence of left ventricular outflow through the subpulmonary VSD to the pulmonary artery
Clinical signs of cyanosis in the neonatal period

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both great arteries arising from the right ventricle with a subpulmonary ventricular septal defect confirmed by echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac MRI and cardiac catheterization may be used for further anatomical delineation and surgical planning.

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of lips and mucous membranes due to right-to-left shunting

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic murmur due to VSD and outflow tract obstruction
pathognomonic.notes: Harsh systolic murmur best heard at the left lower sternal border
searchTerms: murmur due to hole in heart

common.notes: Rapid breathing due to pulmonary overcirculation or heart failure
Due to increased metabolic demand and heart failure
Growth retardation secondary to chronic hypoxia and cardiac insufficiency

occasional.notes: Shortness of breath on feeding or activity
Occasional supraventricular tachycardia or ventricular arrhythmias
Enlarged liver due to right heart failure
Secondary to increased pulmonary blood flow

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits secondary to paradoxical embolism
rare.notes: Stroke or transient ischemic attacks due to right-to-left shunting
Infective endocarditis due to abnormal cardiac anatomy
Bone and joint changes related to chronic hypoxia

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating both great arteries arising from the right ventricle and subpulmonary VSD
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with chromosomal anomalies such as 22q11 deletion syndrome
other: Cardiac catheterization to assess pulmonary pressures and anatomy prior to surgery

distinguishingFeatures: Overriding aorta arises from both ventricles
Absence of both great arteries arising solely from right ventricle
Aorta arises from right ventricle and pulmonary artery from left ventricle
Absence of VSD or presence of non-subpulmonary VSD
Parallel rather than side-by-side great arteries

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
references: Anderson RH, et al. Double outlet right ventricle: anatomical and clinical considerations. Heart. 2014.
Moller JH, et al. Congenital Heart Disease in Infants and Children. 2019.
Orphanet: Double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect (ORPHA:99045)
